Pop Out removes your own bottom checker from a column. Pieces above it fall down. Try popping the highlighted column, or make a regular drop.
You have 20 seconds for each move. Check the board first, then choose where to drop. If time runs out, the move is made for you.
Pieces fade after a few turns. Long-press a column to peek at hidden pieces; peeking costs no move or hint.
Choose the bomb in your piece controls, then drop it. It clears itself and the eight neighboring cells; pieces above fall into the gaps.
The wildcard counts for either player when forming a line. Use it to complete your own line or interrupt your rival’s plan.
Drop a lock piece to secure its column for your rival’s next turn. It cannot trap them when it would leave no legal move.
This larger board needs five connected pieces to win. Build a line across, up and down, or diagonally, and watch for the rival doing the same.
A puzzle limits your own moves. Complete a line within the limit shown above.
Pieces stack in each column. Try the highlighted column and watch where your piece lands.
A central position can create lines in more directions. Compare the highlighted move with the rest of the board.
Before each move, check whether your rival can complete a line. Block immediate threats when you cannot win.
Build your line without leaving an immediate win for the rival. The marker shows one possibility.
In puzzles, the counter counts your moves, not the replies from the rival. Try completing this line.
